rule.sl:
Dodatek prosi sogovornika, naj pritrdi: **It's cold, isn't it?** (Mraz je, a ne?) Pritrdilni stavek, nikalni dodatek; nikalni stavek, pritrdilni dodatek: **It isn't far, is it?** Vzemi pomožni glagol iz stavka: **You've been to Keswick, haven't you?** **It'll rain, won't it?** Brez njega do, does, did: **You live here, don't you?** **Jack saw it, didn't he?**

Posebej: **I'm late, aren't I?** (na Škotskem in Irskem tudi *amn't I*). **There's a bus, isn't there?** **Let's go, shall we?** **Close the door, will you?** **Nobody came, did they?** Ljudje rečejo tudi *innit*, v Walesu in Indiji *isn't it* za vse osebe; v pisanju je dodatek, ki se ujema. Glas pada: pričakuješ da. Glas se dvigne: res sprašuješ.

Pritrditev: **So do I.** **So am I.** **Neither do I.** **Neither can I.** Rečejo tudi **Me too.** in **Me neither.**

Kratek odgovor: **Yes, I do.** **No, she hasn't.** Začudenje: **I've been to Leeds. — Have you?**
rule.de:
Der Anhang bittet den anderen um Zustimmung: **It's cold, isn't it?** (Es ist kalt, oder?) Bejahter Satz, verneinter Anhang; verneinter Satz, bejahter Anhang: **It isn't far, is it?** Nimm das Hilfsverb aus dem Satz: **You've been to Keswick, haven't you?** **It'll rain, won't it?** Ohne Hilfsverb do, does, did: **You live here, don't you?** **Jack saw it, didn't he?**

Besonders: **I'm late, aren't I?** (in Schottland und Irland auch *amn't I*). **There's a bus, isn't there?** **Let's go, shall we?** **Close the door, will you?** **Nobody came, did they?** Man sagt auch *innit*, in Wales und Indien *isn't it* für alle Personen; geschrieben steht der passende Anhang. Stimme fällt: Du erwartest ein Ja. Stimme steigt: Du fragst wirklich.

Zustimmen: **So do I.** **So am I.** **Neither do I.** **Neither can I.** Man sagt auch **Me too.** und **Me neither.**

Kurzantwort: **Yes, I do.** **No, she hasn't.** Staunen: **I've been to Leeds. — Have you?**
rule.it:
La coda chiede all'altro di essere d'accordo: **It's cold, isn't it?** (Fa freddo, vero?) Frase positiva, coda negativa; frase negativa, coda positiva: **It isn't far, is it?** Prendi l'ausiliare dalla frase: **You've been to Keswick, haven't you?** **It'll rain, won't it?** Senza ausiliare do, does, did: **You live here, don't you?** **Jack saw it, didn't he?**

Casi speciali: **I'm late, aren't I?** (in Scozia e Irlanda anche *amn't I*). **There's a bus, isn't there?** **Let's go, shall we?** **Close the door, will you?** **Nobody came, did they?** Si dice anche *innit*, in Galles e in India *isn't it* per tutte le persone; per iscritto la coda che corrisponde. La voce scende: ti aspetti un sì. La voce sale: chiedi davvero.

Essere d'accordo: **So do I.** **So am I.** **Neither do I.** **Neither can I.** Si dice anche **Me too.** e **Me neither.**

Risposta breve: **Yes, I do.** **No, she hasn't.** Stupore: **I've been to Leeds. — Have you?**
rule.en:
A tag asks the other person to agree: **It's cold, isn't it?** A yes sentence, a no tag; a no sentence, a yes tag: **It isn't far, is it?** Take the helping verb from the sentence: **You've been to Keswick, haven't you?** **It'll rain, won't it?** With none, do, does, did: **You live here, don't you?** **Jack saw it, didn't he?**

Special: **I'm late, aren't I?** (in Scotland and Ireland also *amn't I*). **There's a bus, isn't there?** **Let's go, shall we?** **Close the door, will you?** **Nobody came, did they?** People also say *innit*, and in Wales and India *isn't it* for every person; writing wants the tag that fits. Voice falling: you expect yes. Voice rising: you really ask.

To agree: **So do I.** **So am I.** **Neither do I.** **Neither can I.** People also say **Me too.** and **Me neither.**

A short answer: **Yes, I do.** **No, she hasn't.** Surprise: **I've been to Leeds. — Have you?**

tip.sl: 💡 Slovenščina ima za vse *a ne?*, angleščina vzame glagol iz stavka: **isn't it**, **don't you**, **won't it**.
tip.de: 💡 Deutsch hat für alles *oder?* oder *nicht wahr?*, Englisch nimmt das Verb aus dem Satz: **isn't it**, **don't you**, **won't it**.
tip.it: 💡 L'italiano ha per tutto *vero?* o *no?*, l'inglese prende il verbo dalla frase: **isn't it**, **don't you**, **won't it**.
tip.en: 💡 Take the sentence's helping verb and turn it round: **It's** → **isn't it**, **It isn't** → **is it**.
